---
title: "Brand and theming"
subtitle: "Figures that match the document around them."
description: "Reading _brand.yml inside a Typst block, and compiling a figure for both the light and the dark side of a page."
# A ```{typst} block looks like an executable cell to Quarto's engine
# detection, which then selects Jupyter and fails for want of a kernel. The
# extension compiles those blocks itself, so the page needs no engine.
engine: markdown
---

A compiled figure is an image, so it keeps the colours it was drawn with.
The extension binds the document brand ahead of every block, as `_typst_render_brand`, so a figure can draw itself in the colours of the page instead.
Two more bindings, `_typst_render_background` and `_typst_render_foreground`, carry the resolved colours.
The [Reference](../reference.qmd#brand-data) describes all three.

## Brand colours

This page uses the pastel brand shared by these documentation sites.
`background: auto` compiles the block once per colour scheme.
The dictionary matches the side being compiled, so the swatches below change with the theme of the page:

```{typst}
//| echo: true
//| background: auto
#let roles = ("primary", "secondary", "tertiary", "success", "info", "warning", "danger")
#let colours = _typst_render_brand.color
#stack(
  dir: ltr,
  spacing: 4pt,
  ..roles
    .filter(role => role in colours)
    .map(role => rect(width: 1.4cm, height: 1.4cm, radius: 3pt, fill: rgb(colours.at(role)))),
)
```

Under `color` are nine semantic roles: `foreground`, `background`, `primary`, `secondary`, `tertiary`, `success`, `info`, `warning`, and `danger`.
Under `typography` are the `base` and `headings` families.

A role the brand does not define stops the compilation, so read an uncertain one with a default:

```typ
#let accent = _typst_render_brand.color.at("tertiary", default: "#888888")
```

## Light and dark

`background` and `foreground` take three shapes: a Typst colour, `auto` to read the brand, or a map with `light` and `dark` keys.
`auto` and a map each carry two values, so the block is compiled twice in HTML output.
The page then shows the image that matches its mode:

````markdown
```{typst}
//| background: auto
//| foreground: auto
#align(center)[#text(size: 14pt)[This box follows the page.]]
```
````

```{typst}
//| background: auto
//| foreground: auto
#align(center)[#text(size: 14pt)[This box follows the page.]]
```

Switch the theme of this page to see the pair swap.

A block option is one line of `//| key: value`, so an explicit light and dark pair is written in the document or project YAML instead, where it becomes the default for every block:

```yaml
extensions:
  typst-render:
    background:
      light: "#FFF6E5"
      dark: "#20232A"
    foreground:
      light: "#20232A"
      dark: "#FFF6E5"
```

## A plotting package

A package that reads `_brand.yml` takes the dictionary directly.
[Gribouille](https://github.com/mcanouil/gribouille) is one, from version 0.7.0:

````markdown
```{typst}
#import "@preview/gribouille:0.7.0": *

#plot(
  data: (x: (1, 2, 3, 4), y: (2, 4, 3, 5), g: ("a", "b", "a", "b")),
  mapping: aes(x: "x", y: "y", colour: "g"),
  layers: (geom-point(size: 5pt),),
  theme: theme-brand(_typst_render_brand),
  width: 8cm,
  height: 5cm,
)
```
````

The [Reference](../reference.qmd#brand-data) also describes what a brand written for one mode alone does in the other.
